#Dwarf Medicine
Dwarfs use a more detailed medical system called DwarfMed. If you are playing a dwarf, this page is for you. If you are not a dwarf, most of this does not apply.
Your body is split into zones, and each zone can be hurt, broken, or lost separately. Your overall health still decides whether you are alive, critical, or dead.
##The three rules - [bold]Your body takes all the damage.[/bold] A limb is not extra health and does not protect you. - [bold]The body selector chooses the zone.[/bold] It is in the bottom right. It starts on Chest. It decides where your attacks land and where your treatments go. - [bold]Limb damage and body damage are different.[/bold] Body damage can kill you. Limb damage can break a bone or take the limb off.
##Health and limb trauma - You become [bold]Critical at 100 total damage[/bold] and [bold]die at 200[/bold]. - When you are hit, your body takes the full hit. The selected zone also records [bold]half of that hit[/bold] as limb trauma. - Slash, blunt/piercing, and burn trauma are tracked separately. - When a zone has taken enough of one kind of trauma, it can be [bold]severed[/bold]. - Chest and Groin cannot be severed. Everything else can. - Losing a limb does not directly damage you, but the stump bleeds and you lose the use of that limb. - Fire and explosions can damage several zones at once. Fire can burn a limb off completely.
##The body selector - Click a zone on the bottom-right body to select it: Head, Chest, Groin, arms, hands, legs, or feet. - Your selected zone is where [bold]your[/bold] attacks land. - If you are a medic, your selected zone is also the zone you treat with kits, splints, and limb healing. - If the selected part is missing, the game falls back to the nearest part: hand to arm, foot to leg, then chest. - [bold]Check your selector.[/bold] If it is stuck on Left Hand, you will keep aiming at left hands.
##Fractures - Caused by slash and blunt damage. Burn does not fracture. - Signs: a crack sound, dropping your weapon, or moving slowly. - A splint stops the bad effects but [bold]does not heal the fracture[/bold]. - Only Bone Repair surgery fixes a fracture. - Do not run on an unsplinted broken leg. It can start internal bleeding.
##Internal bleeding - Caused by heavy blunt damage to the head, chest, or groin, or by moving on an unsplinted fracture. - Signs: a deep, wet pain and ongoing blood loss. - Gauze, ointment, and trauma kits [bold]do not stop it[/bold]. - Only Internal Bleeding surgery with a Fix-O-Vein stops it.
##Stump bleeding - Happens when a limb is severed. - Pack the stump with gauze or a trauma kit to slow it down. - Packing [bold]does not stop it[/bold]. Only Seal Stump surgery stops it. - Ignored stump bleeding will kill you.
##Organ damage - Organs are in the head, chest, and groin. Big hits to those zones, explosions, and poison can damage them. - Damage is tracked per organ. A badly damaged organ can [bold]rupture[/bold]. - [bold]Heart:[/bold] causes breathlessness and blood loss. A ruptured heart blocks defibrillation until it is repaired. - [bold]Lungs:[/bold] causes suffocation. A ruptured lung suffocates you quickly. - [bold]Brain:[/bold] causes stuttering, jittering, and knockout. A ruptured or missing brain makes you unrevivable. - [bold]Eyes:[/bold] blur your vision, then blind you. - [bold]Kidneys and liver:[/bold] poison you over time. - [bold]Stomach:[/bold] slows how fast food and drink work. - Chems do not repair organs. Organ Repair surgery with the matching gel does.
##Checking injuries - Click the body status alert to check yourself. It reports each zone, for example: "Your left arm is fractured and bleeding internally." - Use a [bold]health analyzer[/bold] on a patient. The body map shows damage, fractures, and bleeding. - The body scanner and medical records also report fractures, internal bleeding, and organ damage. - Tell your medic which zone hurts. It saves time.
##If you are the patient - Tell the medic what hit you and which zone hurts. - Stay still while being treated. Most treatments are do-afters and cancel if you move. - Do not run on a fractured leg or foot. - If a limb comes off, keep it if you can. It can be reattached later. - Do not expect chems to fix a limb, a fracture, or an organ. - A defibrillator is not free: each defib adds heart damage. A ruptured heart or a dead brain cannot be defibbed.
##If you are the medic - [bold]1.[/bold] Select the zone you want to treat on your body selector. - [bold]2.[/bold] Scan the patient and read the injured zones. - [bold]3.[/bold] Treat limb trauma with a trauma kit for slash/blunt or a burn kit for burn. - [bold]4.[/bold] Splint fractures. Pack bleeding stumps. - [bold]5.[/bold] Do surgery for fractures, internal bleeding, stump bleeding, and organ damage. - [bold]6.[/bold] Reattach a severed limb or install a prosthetic when the patient is stable. - An [bold]autodoc[/bold] can handle internal bleeding, broken bones, organ damage, and limb trauma if it has the right upgrades.
##Surgery basics - Most DwarfMed surgeries follow the same pattern: open with a scalpel, clamp with a hemostat, retract with a retractor, do the special step, then close with a cautery. - [bold]Bone Repair:[/bold] apply bone gel with a gel inserter, then use a bone setter. - [bold]Internal Bleeding:[/bold] use a Fix-O-Vein. - [bold]Seal Stump:[/bold] use a Fix-O-Vein. - [bold]Organ Repair:[/bold] apply 5u of the matching organ gel with a gel inserter. - [bold]Amputation:[/bold] use a circular saw. This also drops the hand or foot below the limb. - [bold]Limb Reattachment:[/bold] hold the severed limb during the reattachment step. - [bold]Prosthetic Install:[/bold] hold the matching prosthetic during the install step. - Surgery uses the surgery menu's part selection. It does not use your body selector.
##Gels - The gel inserter holds 5u. - Organ repair needs [bold]exactly 5u of the one correct gel[/bold]. Mixed gels count as the wrong gel. - Wrong organ gel consumes the gel, adds 5 organ damage, and poisons the patient. - Wrong bone gel is wasted, but does not hurt the patient. - Gels: bone, heart, lung, brain, eye, kidney, liver, and stomach.
##Prosthetics - Prosthetic limbs replace missing arms, hands, legs, and feet. - They do not fracture, do not get internal bleeding, and do not bleed from stumps. - Repair a prosthetic's brute damage with a blowtorch, and its burn damage with a cable coil. - You cannot replace a brain. Brain removal is permanent.
##Common mistakes - Using chems on a limb and expecting the limb trauma to go down. Chems heal the body only. - Splinting a fracture and thinking it is fixed. It is only braced. - Packing a stump and thinking the bleeding is stopped. It is only slowed. - Mixing gels. Use one gel at a time. - Forgetting the body selector. It affects both attacks and treatment. - Trying to amputate the chest or groin. They cannot be removed. - Defibbing a patient with a ruptured heart or a dead brain. Repair the organ first, or do not expect a revive.
